links.outcome: Model AUC across racial/ethnic, age, and income subgroups versus overall
links.effect: Overall AUC 0.84; full model AUC 0.88 for White individuals and older adults, with performance loss for other subgroups; lowest AUC 0.76 for other/multiple racial groups.
links.quote: While the full sample model performed similarly when applied to White individuals and older adults (AUC, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.87-0.90), there was a loss of performance for other subgroups.

links.outcome: Model performance after removing race/ethnicity, age, and income predictors
links.effect: Removing subgroup-sensitive predictors (race and ethnicity, age, income) did not impact model performance.
links.quote: Removing the subgroup-sensitive predictors (ie, race and ethnicity, age, and income) did not impact model performance.

unlisted_practices: Fitting race/ethnicity-stratified models compared with a full-sample model (stratified models performed similarly or worse)

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates algorithmic fairness and bias across sociodemographic subgroups in predictive risk modeling for dental care, including testing the effect of removing subgroup-sensitive predictors and stratifying models.

primary.practice: algorithmic fairness evaluation and subgroup stratification
